solutions.explanation:
Subtracting the expressions reveals exactly when they are equal. Expanding and collecting terms gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
(a+b)(a+c)-(a+bc)
&=a^2+ab+ac+bc-a-bc\\
&=a(a+b+c-1).
\end{aligned}
\]
This product is zero precisely when \(a=0\) or \(a+b+c=1\). We have not divided by \(a\), so the case \(a=0\) is retained.

In particular, whenever \(a+b+c=1\), the expressions are equal. The word “when” states a sufficient condition, so it allows equality in other cases too. The correct choice is \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).
solutions.title: Compare the expressions by subtraction
